findings.effort: A column in stops.txt; your scheduling software likely has it.
findings.fix: Set wheelchair_boarding to 1 (accessible) or 2 (not accessible) for every stop. A field survey can start with the busiest stops.
findings.what: 918 of 918 stops don't say whether a wheelchair user can board there.
findings.why: Riders who use wheelchairs can't plan a trip when accessibility is marked 'unknown'; apps show no information at all.

findings.effort: A default or per-trip field in your export.
findings.fix: Set wheelchair_accessible on every trip. If every vehicle is accessible, this may be one default; otherwise use the value for each trip.
findings.what: 6546 of 6546 trips don't say whether the vehicle is wheelchair accessible.
findings.why: Even with accessible stops, riders need to know the bus itself can take them.

findings.effort: Often a bulk fix in your scheduling software.
findings.fix: Rename stops to mixed case where the language has letter case (for example, 'Central Station').
findings.what: About 880 stop names are written in ALL CAPS.
findings.why: Mixed-case names are easier to read in apps and are read more naturally by screen readers.

findings.what: feed_info.txt has no technical contact (feed_contact_email or feed_contact_url).
findings.why: Trip-planning apps and regional data coordinators have nobody to email when they spot a problem with your feed, so problems linger.

completeness.name: completeness
completeness.summary: 0% of stops state wheelchair accessibility (0% marked accessible, 0% marked not accessible). This measures what the feed publishes, not whether a stop is physically usable. Fare data is published.

findings.fix: Review the rule documentation for 'duplicate_key' at https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/rules.html and check the flagged rows in your feed.
findings.what: Duplicate key (flagged by the MobilityData validator).
findings.why: See the linked rule for what this affects.

findings.effort: Often a bulk fix in your scheduling software.
findings.fix: Use mixed case for stop names and headsigns (e.g. 'Main St & 2nd Ave', not 'MAIN ST & 2ND AVE').
findings.what: Some rider-facing names are in ALL CAPS or all lowercase.
findings.why: ALL-CAPS stop and headsign names are harder to read in apps and are read awkwardly by screen readers.

findings.effort: Usually an export-tool fix, not hand editing.
findings.fix: Check the flagged stops' shape_dist_traveled against the route shape, and re-generate it on export if they disagree.
findings.what: Some stops sit far from the route line, going by the feed's own distance values.
findings.why: Trip planners may draw the route down the wrong streets or point riders to the wrong corner.

findings.fix: Give each route a distinct short or long name.
findings.what: Two or more routes share the same name.
findings.why: Riders can't tell the routes apart in apps.

findings.effort: A few minutes per flagged trip.
findings.fix: Check the stop order and the shape direction in your scheduling software; the shape is often drawn backwards.
findings.what: On some trips the stops fall along the route line in a different order than the schedule lists.
findings.why: Trip planners can draw the bus doubling back or skipping ahead, which confuses riders reading the map.

findings.effort: A field at a time; not urgent.
findings.fix: Review the flagged fields and fill in the ones your riders would use.
findings.what: Some files leave out fields that GTFS asks for but does not require.
findings.why: Recommended fields like agency_phone or stop descriptions make the feed more useful to riders and trip planners.

findings.effort: One field, set once in export settings.
findings.fix: Add feed_contact_email or feed_contact_url to feed_info.txt.
findings.what: feed_info.txt lists no contact email and no contact URL.
findings.why: Without a contact, apps like Google Maps can't reach you when they find a problem in the feed.

findings.effort: A quick look at the flagged file.
findings.fix: Check the flagged file name for a typo of a standard GTFS file. Remove it if it is a vendor extra.
findings.what: The feed includes a file that is not part of the GTFS spec.
findings.why: Apps ignore files they don't know, and a stray file can hide a misspelled standard file name.

correctness.summary: The MobilityData validator flagged 8 kinds of issue across 1132 instances (34 error, 1096 warning, 2 informational).

freshness.name: freshness
freshness.summary: Service data covers the next 127 days.

findings.effort: A vendor support ticket; treat it as a feed outage.
findings.fix: Ask your AVL vendor why the feed stopped advancing; the GTFS-Realtime header timestamp should move forward on every publish.
findings.what: The realtime feed's last update was about 483 days old when sampled.
findings.why: A realtime feed this far behind has effectively stopped. Riders see buses that already left, or apps quietly fall back to the schedule while still showing a live label.

findings.fix: Check with your AVL vendor that every vehicle assignment flows into TripUpdates, including school-day and tripper runs.
findings.what: 90 of 90 trips scheduled during the sampling window had no live predictions.
findings.why: Riders on those trips get schedule data dressed up as realtime. Caltrans expects every operating trip in TripUpdates.

ntd_id_alignment.detail: Your feed's agency_id is 6216179; your National Transit Database ID is 90008. A feed that serves several agencies (a shared regional feed) can legitimately carry more than one agency_id. The values do not need to equal the five-digit NTD ID, so this difference is allowed and carries no score.
ntd_id_alignment.fix: Confirm that P-50 crosswalks agency_id 6216179 to NTD ID 90008, and keep the feed value stable. Do not change it solely to make the two values equal.

pillars.detail: Service data covers the next 129 days.
agency.txt provides agency_id. For RY2026, keep one stable value for each NTD reporter represented in the feed and crosswalk each value on the P-50 form.

ntd_readiness.summary: This feed is close to NTD-ready. 1 validator error to resolve.

recommendations.effort: A per-route color setting in your scheduling software.
recommendations.fix: Adjust route_color or route_text_color so each pair clears 4.5:1. Often switching the text between black and white is enough.
recommendations.what: 4 route badge(s) pair a color and text color below the WCAG 4.5:1 contrast bar (R10, 43, R10, 43).
recommendations.why: Low-contrast route badges are hard to read for riders with low vision and wash out on a phone screen in sunlight at the stop.

recommendations.effort: A short text field per affected stop; start with the busiest.
recommendations.fix: Add tts_stop_name with the spoken form, e.g. 'Main Street and Second Avenue', for the affected stops.
recommendations.what: 908 stop name(s) use abbreviations or symbols a screen reader may mispronounce, with no spoken form set ("4TH NB & SANTA MONICA NS", "SANTA MONICA EB & 6TH NS", "SANTA MONICA EB & CENTINELA FS", and more).
recommendations.why: Riders who use a screen reader hear the raw name, so 'Main St & 2nd Ave' can come out as 'Main saint' or drop the ampersand.
